vulnerability.name: CVE-2026-84304
vulnerability.description: gRPC-go: heap memory exhaustion via HTTP/2 DATA frame fragmentation

statements.status_notes: Fixed by Trivy v0.76.0 (TRIVY_VERSION in Containerfile.worker), built with Go 1.27.2 against grpc-go v1.84.0; its .trivyignore.yaml entry was removed with the bump. Worker images published before this change carried the vulnerable binary only as a client of the chart's Trivy server and were stated not_affected in version 1 of this document.

statements.status_notes: Fixed in 1.8.1: rustls-webpki 0.103.16 and webpki-roots / webpki-root-certs 1.0.10 in the server, which verifies upstream TLS with them, and Trivy v0.76.1 (TRIVY_VERSION in Containerfile.worker), built with Go 1.27.3, in the worker images. 1.8.0 and earlier carry the affected versions.

vulnerability.name: CVE-2026-116587
vulnerability.description: go-jose: denial of service via crafted RSA parameters in JWKs

statements.impact_statement: The vulnerable go-jose is an indirect dependency of the upstream Trivy release binary the worker image carries (/usr/local/bin/trivy, pinned by TRIVY_VERSION in Containerfile.worker), not of any BatleHub code. Trivy reaches JWK parsing only through its sigstore/Rekor attestation paths (`--sbom-sources rekor`, attestation verification), which are opt-in; the worker runs it as `trivy ... --server <endpoint>` (crates/adapters/src/scanners/trivy.rs) and never passes those flags, so no JWK from an untrusted source is parsed.
statements.action_statement: Bump TRIVY_VERSION to the first Trivy release whose go.mod carries go-jose/v4 >= 4.1.6 (Trivy main already does; v0.76.1 does not), and delete this statement together with its .trivyignore.yaml entry.
